result: Establishes a complete classification of subalgebra QCAs on 1D spin systems with finite Abelian group symmetry, and shows the Kramers-Wannier duality has an irrational index and cannot be extended to a full QCA.
conclusion: Provides a rigorous classification framework for symmetric quantum cellular automata, revealing connections to anyon permutations and topological order.

title: On The Significance Of Wigner’s Friend In Contexts Beyond Quantum Foundations
authors: Caroline L. Jones And Markus P. Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2147 (2026).

There has been a surge of recent interest in the Wigner's Friend paradox, sparking several novel thought experiments and no-go theorems. The main narrative has been that Wigner's Friend highlights a counterintuitive feature that is unique to quantum theory, and which is closely related to the quantum measurement problem. Here, we challenge this view. We argue that the gist of the Wigner's Friend paradox can be reproduced without assuming quantum physics, and that it underlies a much broader class of enigmas in the foundations of physics and philosophy. To show this, we first consider several recently proposed Extended Wigner's Friend scenarios, and demonstrate that some of their implications for the absoluteness of observations can be reproduced by classical thought experiments that involve the duplication of agents. Crucially, some of these classical scenarios are technologically much easier to implement than their quantum counterparts. Then, we argue that the essential structural ingredient of all these scenarios is a feature that we call "Restriction A": that a physical theory cannot give us a probabilistic description of the observations of all agents. Finally, we argue that this difficulty is at the core of other puzzles in the foundations of physics and philosophy, and demonstrate this explicitly for cosmology's Boltzmann brain problem. Our analysis suggests that Wigner's Friend should be studied in a larger context, addressing a frontier of human knowledge beyond quantum foundations: to obtain reliable predictions for experiments in which these predictions can be privately but not intersubjectively verified.

.
tldr: This paper argues that the Wigner's Friend paradox is not unique to quantum theory but can be reproduced classically, and it connects the paradox to broader foundational issues like the Boltzmann brain problem.
motivation: The authors challenge the prevailing view that Wigner's Friend highlights a uniquely quantum feature, aiming to show that the core paradox arises from a general restriction on probabilistic descriptions of observations.
method: They analyze extended Wigner's Friend scenarios and construct classical thought experiments with agent duplication to reproduce the paradox, then identify a structural feature called 'Restriction A' that underlies these puzzles.
result: They demonstrate that some implications of Wigner's Friend can be reproduced classically, and that the essential ingredient is a limitation on intersubjective verification, which also appears in cosmology's Boltzmann brain problem.
conclusion: Wigner's Friend should be studied in a broader context beyond quantum foundations, as it addresses a general frontier of knowledge where predictions cannot be intersubjectively verified.

title: Qubit Operations Using A Modular Optical System Engineered With PyOpticL: A code-to-CAD Optical Layout Tool
authors: Jacob Myers, Christopher Caron, Nishat Helaly, Zhenyu Wei, Justin Oh, Zack Gotobed, Kotaro Yabe, And Robert J. Niffenegger
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2135 (2026).

Complex optical design is hindered by conventional piecewise setup, which prevents modularization and therefore abstraction of subsystems at the circuit level. This limits multiple fields that require complex optics systems, including quantum computing with atoms and trapped ions, because their optical systems are not scalable. We present an open-source Python library for optical layout (PyOpticL) which uses beam-path simulation and dynamic beam-path routing for quick and easy optical layout by placing optical elements along the beam path without a priori specification, enabling adaptive, path-based layouts with automatic routing and connectivity. We use PyOpticL to create modular `drop-in' optical baseplates for common optical subsystems used in atomic and molecular optics (AMO) experiments including laser sources, frequency and intensity modulation, and locking to an atomic reference for stabilization. We demonstrate this minimal working example of a dynamic full laser system for strontium trapped ions by using it for laser cooling, qubit state detection, and over 99% fidelity single-qubit gates with 3D printed baseplates. This enables a new paradigm of design abstraction layers for engineering optical systems leveraging modular baseplates, as they can be used for any wavelength in the system and enables scaling up the underlying optical systems for quantum computers. This new open-source hardware and software code-to-CAD library seeks to foster open-source collaborative hardware and systems design across numerous fields of research including AMO physics and quantum computing with neutral atoms and trapped ions.

.
tldr: Presents an open-source Python library for optical layout and demonstrates modular optical baseplates for trapped-ion quantum computing.
motivation: Complex optical design in quantum computing with atoms and trapped ions is not scalable due to conventional piecewise setup.
method: Developed PyOpticL, a Python library using beam-path simulation and dynamic routing, and created modular drop-in optical baseplates for common subsystems.
result: Demonstrated a full laser system for strontium trapped ions achieving over 99% fidelity single-qubit gates with 3D printed baseplates.
conclusion: Enables a new paradigm of design abstraction layers for engineering optical systems, fostering open-source collaborative hardware design.

title: Readjustment Of Intrinsic Activity Parameters Governs The Rectified Transport In Asymmetric Ratchets
authors: Yunyan Chen, Xiaoyuan Yu, Fengguo Li And Baoquan Ai
abstract: The rectified transport of active Brownian particles (ABPs) in asymmetric ratchets has been extensively studied. However, most existing literature regulates rectification by designing different structural boundaries. In this work, we shift the research perspective to the internal properties of ABPs and explore the influence of their internal physical parameters on the transport process. Using the vibration-driven vehicle (VDV) as a macroscopic experimental model for ABPs, we systematically adjust the overall mass and position of center of mass of the VDV to reveal its underlying dynamic mechanism. Through long-time dynamic tracking, we identify a ‘parameters readjustment effect’: an increase in mass weakens the particle’s average velocity and persistence length, ultimately driving the active system into a noise-dominated macroscopic localized state. More importantly, the shift of the center of mass induces persistent translational–rotational coupling in the VDV, leading to an anomalous non-monotonic reentrant phase transition in the rectification probability of the system. Our study reveals that this anomalous transport law is fundamentally governed by the dynamic spatial competition between the intrinsic chiral orbit radius of the VDV and the geometric characteristic scale of the channel. Coarse-grained ABP numerical simulations reproduce the overall experimental trends. This work indicates that load-induced parameters evolution is not merely a physical perturbation, but a core dimension that determines macroscopic transport behavior, providing physical insights and principles for going beyond purely geometric design constraints and designing efficient active rectification systems.
tldr: This paper studies rectified transport of active Brownian particles in asymmetric ratchets by adjusting internal parameters like mass and center of mass, using a macroscopic experimental model.
motivation: Most existing work regulates rectification via structural boundaries; this paper shifts focus to internal properties of active particles to understand their influence on transport.
method: A vibration-driven vehicle (VDV) serves as a macroscopic model for active Brownian particles; mass and center of mass are systematically varied, and long-time dynamics are tracked experimentally and via coarse-grained simulations.
result: Increasing mass weakens average velocity and persistence length, leading to a noise-dominated localized state; shifting the center of mass induces translational-rotational coupling causing a non-monotonic reentrant phase transition in rectification probability.
conclusion: Load-induced parameter evolution is a core determinant of macroscopic transport behavior, offering principles for designing efficient active rectification systems beyond geometric constraints.

title: Classical Field Simulation Of Vortex Lattice Melting In A Two-dimensional Fast Rotating Bose Gas
authors: Sálvio J Bereta, Lucas Madeira, Mônica A Caracanhas, Hélène Perrin And Romain Dubessy
abstract: We present a classical field simulation study of the thermal melting of a two-dimensional (2D) vortex lattice in a rotating Bose gas, focusing on the role of finite-size effects on the melting temperature. This work constitutes a numerical continuation of the recent experimental investigation reported in (Sharma 2024 Phys. Rev. Lett.133 143401), which addressed the thermal melting of a vortex lattice in a quasi-2D Bose gas. Using the stochastic projected Gross–Pitaevskii equation in a harmonic plus quartic trap, we simulate the finite-temperature equilibrium state and extract vortex configurations from density snapshots. Clear signatures of the two-step Kosterlitz–Thouless–Halperin–Nelson–Young melting scenario are identified. Our simulations enable a detailed characterization of the crystalline, hexatic, and liquid phases through correlation functions quantifying the translational and orientational order and through defect statistics. Finite-size effects are shown to play a crucial role at lower rotation frequencies, affecting the proliferation of lattice defects.
tldr: Classical field simulation of vortex lattice melting in a rotating Bose gas, focusing on finite-size effects.
motivation: To understand the thermal melting of vortex lattices in two-dimensional Bose gases, which is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: Uses the stochastic projected Gross–Pitaevskii equation to simulate finite-temperature equilibrium states and extract vortex configurations.
result: Identifies a two-step Kosterlitz–Thouless–Halperin–Nelson–Young melting scenario and shows that finite-size effects significantly affect the melting temperature at lower rotation frequencies.
conclusion: The simulations provide detailed characterization of crystalline, hexatic, and liquid phases, highlighting the importance of finite-size effects.

title: Direct Derivation Of The Modified Langevin Noise Formalism From The Canonical Quantization Of Macroscopic Electromagnetism
authors: A Ciattoni
abstract: The modified Langevin noise formalism (MLNF) models the interaction of the quantized electromagnetic field with an arbitrary lossy magneto-dielectric object placed in vacuum using three types of non-interacting bosonic polaritons: scattering, electric, and magnetic. These respectively represent free-space photons scattered by the object, and photons radiated by quantized electric and magnetic dipolar sources embedded within its volume. Recently (Ciattoni 2024 Phys. Rev. A110 013707), this formalism was justified from the canonical quantization of macroscopic electromagnetism (CQME) (Philbin 2010 New J. Phys.12 123008) in the Heisenberg picture. This was achieved by identifying the polariton operators within the formal solution of the macroscopic Maxwell equations, assuming they obey bosonic commutation relations to retrieve the canonical ones, and showing they diagonalize the CQME Hamiltonian. However, the explicit functional dependence of these polaritons on the underlying canonical field operators remained undetermined. In this paper, we derive the exact analytical expressions for the polariton operators in terms of the canonical CQME field operators. Using these mappings, we provide a direct and rigorous derivation of the MLNF from the canonical theory in the Schrödinger picture. Our derivation is structured in three foundational steps: 1) adopting the derived analytical expressions as the constitutive definitions of the polariton operators; 2) mathematically proving that these operators are strictly bosonic as a direct consequence of the canonical commutation relations; and 3) demonstrating that they exactly diagonalize the macroscopic CQME Hamiltonian.
tldr: This paper derives exact analytical expressions for polariton operators in the modified Langevin noise formalism from canonical quantization of macroscopic electromagnetism.
motivation: To provide a rigorous derivation of the modified Langevin noise formalism (MLNF) from canonical quantization of macroscopic electromagnetism (CQME) by explicitly expressing polariton operators in terms of canonical field operators.
method: The authors adopt analytical expressions as constitutive definitions of polariton operators, prove they satisfy bosonic commutation relations from canonical ones, and show they diagonalize the CQME Hamiltonian.
result: Exact mappings between polariton operators and canonical field operators are obtained, providing a direct derivation of MLNF in the Schrödinger picture.
conclusion: The MLNF is rigorously derived from first principles, confirming its consistency with canonical quantization of macroscopic electromagnetism.

title: A Frequency-domain Identifiability Law For Deterministic Reconstruction Of Complex Networks Under Partial Observability
authors: Tianlong Fan And Linyuan Lü Xiaoxiao Liang
abstract: Inferring network architecture from partial behavioral observations is central to computational studies of complex systems, with implications for detecting covert actors in terrorist networks, localizing unobserved brain regions, and revealing latent molecular regulators. Focusing on evolutionary game dynamics, we uncover an empirically consistent frequency-domain regularity: the aggregated magnitude of the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) of a node’s payoff time series scales linearly with its structural degree, , across tested topologies and parameter regimes. Leveraging this structure–behavior scaling, we develop a deterministic inference framework that (i) estimates degrees directly from DFT spectra via a single global-slope fit, and (ii) uses brief, identifiability-oriented local interventions (‘suppress-and-measure’) to reveal adjacencies through intervention-induced spectral drops. Discrepancies between estimated degree and revealed neighbors deterministically enumerate external edges to hidden components and yield tight lower/upper bounds on the number of unobserved nodes. We analyze the conditions under which the scaling holds, quantify deviations under structural heterogeneity, and characterize sample-length dependence. Experiments on synthetic and empirical networks demonstrate accurate topology recovery, robustness to stochasticity, and scalability to thousand-node graphs, with consistent gains over causality-, correlation-, information-, and likelihood-based baselines. These results establish a DFT-based route to structure discovery under partial observability, translating local spectral measurements into actionable structural information.
tldr: This paper presents a frequency-domain method for inferring network structure from partial observations of evolutionary game dynamics.
motivation: Inferring network architecture from partial behavioral data is important for detecting covert actors, localizing brain regions, and revealing molecular regulators.
method: The authors discover a linear scaling between the DFT magnitude of payoff time series and node degree, and develop a deterministic inference framework using spectral measurements and local interventions.
result: The method accurately recovers network topology on synthetic and empirical networks, outperforming causality-, correlation-, and likelihood-based baselines.
conclusion: The DFT-based approach provides a new route to structure discovery under partial observability.

title: Strong Field Ionized Electron Trajectories Driven By Squeezed Light
authors: Alex Schimmoller And Alexandra S Landsman
abstract: In atomic strong field ionization, a photoelectron’s motion is largely determined by the laser pulse’s expected electric field, as well as the atomic potential. However, when the ionization is performed by squeezed light, the photon’s quantum statistics can modify these dynamics. In this work, we generalize the classical trajectory Monte–Carlo technique to study strong field ionization by squeezed states of light. We find that electrons driven by phase-squeezed pulses exhibit increases in longitudinal momentum consistent with what is expected from the field statistics. Meanwhile, the transverse momentum distribution shows varying influence of ‘hard’ and ‘soft’ rescattering off the Coulomb potential, and the proportion of electrons recaptured as Rydberg states decreases monotonically with the amount of squeezed light applied. This work demonstrates the added experimental control over ultrafast electron dynamics achievable by tuning light’s quantum statistics, as well as the essential role of the atomic potential in strong field ionization.
tldr: This paper studies electron trajectories in strong field ionization driven by squeezed light, focusing on the effect of quantum statistics on ultrafast electron dynamics.
motivation: To understand how squeezed light modifies electron dynamics in strong field ionization, potentially offering new control over ultrafast processes.
method: Generalized classical trajectory Monte-Carlo technique to simulate strong field ionization by squeezed states of light.
result: Phase-squeezed pulses increase longitudinal momentum as expected from field statistics; transverse momentum distribution shows varying rescattering effects; Rydberg recapture decreases with squeezing.
conclusion: Squeezed light provides experimental control over ultrafast electron dynamics, and the atomic potential plays an essential role in strong field ionization.

title: Vortex Solitons In Disclination Quasicrystals
authors: Hua Zhong, Yaroslav V Kartashov, Yongdong Li, Fangwei Ye And Yiqi Zhang
abstract: Quasicrystals are ubiquitous in nature. They represent unique aperiodic materials featuring long-range order that occupy an intermediate niche between exactly periodic and disordered materials. These properties are reflected in the unusual evolutionary dynamics of excitations and unique localization properties of linear eigenmodes supported by quasicrystals. In particular, being the structures characterized by discrete rotational symmetry of order , photonic quasicrystals can support the stable propagation of linear vortex-carrying light beams and vortex solitons. However, the impact of discrete rotational symmetry of quasicrystals on the properties of vortex light states has not been investigated so far, as only the systems constructed using the simplest Penrose tiling or corresponding optically induced Penrose lattices are considered in this context. Here, we propose a broad class of quasicrystals with global topological defects—disclinations—introduced into their structure that allows to produce novel quasicrystalline structures with any desired order of discrete rotational symmetry from the basic Penrose structure. Such global topological deformation substantially enriches the linear spectrum of quasicrystals, allowing them to support new types of linear vortex states and bifurcating from them families of stable thresholdless vortex solitons with unusual intensity and phase distributions. We find two different classes of stable vortex solitons comprising in-phase or out-of-phase pairs of closely located bright spots, with total intensity distribution reflecting a particular discrete rotational symmetry of the quasicrystal with disclination. Remarkably, even low-charge vortex solitons can be stable in quasicrystals with disclinations, whereas stability intervals for them broaden with the decrease of the discrete rotational symmetry of quasicrystals. Our results extend the theory of localization in quasicrystals to structures with global topological deformation, highlighting emerging prospects for the robust transmission of power or information arising in these systems.
tldr: This paper studies vortex solitons in photonic quasicrystals with disclinations, focusing on their stability and intensity distributions.
motivation: To understand how global topological defects (disclinations) in quasicrystals affect the properties of vortex light states, which have not been investigated before.
method: The authors propose a class of quasicrystals with disclinations, analyze their linear spectrum, and numerically find families of stable vortex solitons.
result: Two classes of stable vortex solitons are found, with stability intervals broadening as discrete rotational symmetry decreases.
conclusion: The results extend localization theory to quasicrystals with topological deformations, offering potential for robust transmission of power or information.

title: Uniaxial-stress-induced Magnetic Transitions In The Triangular-lattice Antiferromagnet PdCrO2
authors: Nina Stilkerich, Tobias Ritschel, Hilary M L Noad, Richard Waite, Dmitry Khalyavin, Kousuke Ishida, Pascal Manuel, Fabio Orlandi, Seunghyun Khim, Elena Gati, Andrew P Mackenzie, Jochen Geck And Clifford W Hicks
abstract: Uniaxial stress is a promising method to tune magnetic frustration, allowing its effects to be studied in a precise way. In this work, uniaxial stress is applied to the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO . The Cr–Cr magnetic interaction is very sensitive to interatomic separation, so laboratory-achievable stress can induce substantial changes in magnetic structure. Results from three types of measurement are presented: x-ray diffraction, the stress–strain relationship, and neutron diffraction. The combined data show that the elastic moduli of PdCrO are strongly affected by stress-induced changes in magnetic structure. A new, first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, at which the lattice constant shrinks by 0.21%. The lattice stiffens dramatically across this transition: the Young’s modulus increases by GPa, and the Poisson ratio falls from to . This stiffening indicates that the magnetic order ‘locks,’ that is, becomes insensitive to lattice strain. This locking might occur because the new stress-induced magnetic order nests the Fermi surface of the Pd sheets. Other frustrated magnets, including candidate spin liquids, may show similarly strong coupling between magnetic and elastic degrees of freedom.
tldr: This paper studies stress-induced magnetic transitions in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO2, focusing on magnetoelastic coupling.
motivation: To understand how uniaxial stress can tune magnetic frustration and induce new magnetic phases in frustrated magnets.
method: Combined x-ray diffraction, stress-strain measurements, and neutron diffraction under uniaxial stress.
result: A first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, accompanied by a 0.21% lattice shrinkage and dramatic stiffening of the lattice.
conclusion: The magnetic order becomes locked to the lattice, possibly due to Fermi surface nesting, suggesting strong magnetoelastic coupling in frustrated magnets.

title: Direct Visualization Of Field-driven Valence Band Modulation In Electrostatically Reconfigured Graphene Devices
authors: Umidakhon Rayimjonova, Chin-Yi Huang, Yi-Cheng Weng, Elin Cartwright, Fredrik O L Johansson, Noemi Vannucchi, Pavel Dudin, Avila Jose, Pei Ding, David Muradas-Belinchón, Henry Nameirakpam, Zhaojun Li, Andreas Lindblad And M Venkata Kamalakar
abstract: Graphene with ultrathin metal-oxide layers has emerged as a scalable platform for integrated electronic, spintronic, and neuromorphic devices. The in-plane electric fields in such devices are typically inferred indirectly from transport measurements, which do not provide microscopic details of the interface potential profile. Here, we use photoemission microscopy to uncover the precise electrostatic landscape of a complete device comprising diverse, heterogeneous ultrathin metal-oxide-covered graphene junctions. Using in operando x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy with submicron resolution, we directly image the real potential profile across an entire graphene device, including regions covered by AlOx and TiOx nanometer-thick overlayers. Tracking the valence band edge under current bias and gate voltage enables quantitative analysis of internal field evolution via a spectroscopic screening factor, revealing an up to more than 50% suppression of the electric field in graphene covered with oxides, in agreement with transport measurements. This demonstrates local reconfiguration of electric fields in graphene for advanced two-dimensional (2D) device engineering and circuitry, while our operando circuit spectroscopy measurements provide a generic means to uncover intricate potential landscapes and carrier redistribution in 2D electronic and spintronic circuits.
tldr: This paper uses photoemission microscopy to directly visualize the electrostatic potential profile in graphene devices with oxide overlayers, revealing field suppression.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic electrostatic landscape in graphene devices is crucial for optimizing electronic and spintronic performance, but indirect transport measurements lack spatial detail.
method: In operando x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy with submicron resolution was used to image the valence band edge across a graphene device under bias and gate voltage, extracting a spectroscopic screening factor.
result: The electric field in graphene covered with AlOx and TiOx is suppressed by up to 50% compared to bare graphene, consistent with transport measurements.
conclusion: Operando circuit spectroscopy provides a generic method to map potential landscapes in 2D devices, enabling advanced engineering of graphene-based circuits.

tldr: This paper reports a record-high shift current response in ferroelectric halide perovskite CsGeI3, focusing on nonlinear optical properties for photovoltaics.
motivation: Shift current photovoltaics offer a mechanism distinct from conventional p-n junctions, and enhancing the shift current response is crucial for practical applications.
method: The authors measure the shift current response in CsGeI3 and characterize its glass coefficient, likely using optical spectroscopy and first-principles calculations.
result: They achieve a record-high glass coefficient for shift current in this material.
conclusion: CsGeI3 is a promising candidate for shift current-based photovoltaic devices.

title: Deterministic Initiation Of Inner-shell X-ray Lasers By Two-color Raman Driving
authors: Carles Serrat
abstract: Inner-shell x-ray lasers are conventionally initiated by amplified spontaneous emission (ASE), so that the temporal onset and longitudinal phase of the emitted field are determined by microscopic noise fluctuations. As a result, the early-time dynamics of the laser pulse are intrinsically stochastic. We analyze a regime in which the initial polarization that triggers inner-shell x-ray lasing is imposed deterministically by a resonant two-color Raman drive. Two coherent x-ray fields at angular frequencies and satisfying induce a core–valence coherence at the lasing frequency through an off-resonant Raman coupling mediated by virtual intermediate states. No electromagnetic field is applied at , and population inversion is generated independently by conventional inner-shell photoionization. The Raman-driven coherence therefore acts as an intrinsic microscopic seed for stimulated K emission in the linear small-signal regime, without modifying the underlying gain mechanism. This deterministically seeded operating regime will be referred to as resonant x-ray difference-frequency lasing. Within a microscopic density-matrix description coupled to a linear Maxwell–Bloch–Langevin propagation model with calibrated spontaneous-emission noise, we derive an explicit analytical criterion separating a noise-dominated ASE regime from a coherence-dominated seeded regime within a finite temporal overlap window. The criterion depends only on the dimensionless Raman drive amplitude, accumulated small-signal gain, gate duration, and calibrated noise strength. Numerical integration of the stochastic propagation equations in dimensionless form confirms the predicted crossover for the same parameter set used in the analytical criterion. These results identify a coherence-dominated operating regime of inner-shell x-ray lasing in which the origin of the amplified field is shifted from spontaneous fluctuations to a driven microscopic coherence, while the gain dynamics remain unchanged. The mechanism requires two-color x-ray fields with a well-defined relative phase within each shot over the overlap window. A microscopic evaluation of the effective Raman coupling using atomic-structure calculations for Ne provides a quantitative mapping from the analytical threshold to pump intensities. Within a bound-manifold estimate, the corresponding seed-dominance threshold lies in the range – , although this mapping can be shifted by continuum contributions and transient plasma-induced broadening and level shifts not included explicitly in the present model.
tldr: This paper proposes a deterministic seeding mechanism for inner-shell x-ray lasers using two-color Raman driving, shifting the initiation from noise-dominated ASE to a coherence-dominated regime.
motivation: Conventional inner-shell x-ray lasers are initiated by stochastic ASE, leading to unpredictable temporal onset and phase. The authors aim to achieve deterministic control over the lasing initiation.
method: The authors analyze a regime where a resonant two-color Raman drive induces core-valence coherence at the lasing frequency, acting as a seed. They use a microscopic density-matrix description coupled to a linear Maxwell-Bloch-Langevin propagation model with calibrated noise, deriving an analytical criterion for the crossover from ASE to seeded regime.
result: An explicit analytical criterion is derived that separates noise-dominated ASE from coherence-dominated seeded regime, depending on Raman drive amplitude, gain, gate duration, and noise strength. Numerical simulations confirm the predicted crossover.
conclusion: The mechanism enables deterministic initiation of inner-shell x-ray lasing, shifting the field's origin from spontaneous fluctuations to a driven microscopic coherence, without altering the gain dynamics.

title: Characterizing Resources For Multiparameter Estimation Of Su(2) And Su(1,1) Unitaries
authors: Shaowei Du, Shuheng Liu, Frank E. S. Steinhoff, And Giuseppe Vitagliano
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2130 (2026).

We analyze the task of estimating a multi-parameter unitary belonging to the [MATH] or [MATH] groups, in a two-bosonic-mode scenario and investigate the scaling of the precision in terms of the total particle number. For the [MATH] case, the total particle number is conserved by the evolution and we discuss optimal states in fixed-[MATH] subspaces, identifying eigenstates of [MATH] as useful resources, even allowing simultaneous Heisenberg precision scaling for all three parameters. In the [MATH] case instead, the conserved quantity is the particle number difference between the two modes, and we identify useful probe states in the sector with an equal number of particles in the two modes. These states are analogous to the [MATH] case and would also allow simultaneous Heisenberg precision scaling for all three parameters. We then consider the more pragmatic scenario of an estimation via expectation values of time-evolved observables, which we restrict to be the first two moments of the generators. We analyze the maximal precision achievable in this setting and we find that the twin-Fock state emerges in both the [MATH] and the [MATH] cases as the only one potentially allowing Heisenberg scaling for the estimation of two out of the three parameters. As a complement, we also consider other probe states with fluctuating number of particles, with measurements restricted to quadratic expressions in the mode operators. In this scenario, simultaneous Heisenberg scaling in multiple parameters seems mostly forbidden, with the only exception being an input two-mode squeezed state for the estimation of a two-parameter [MATH]. This extends to the multiparameter scenario the well-established intuition that the performance of a [MATH] interferometer can be enhanced by a prior [MATH] operation.

title: Propagation And Collisionless Damping Of Topologically-protected Surface Plasma Waves In Non-uniformly Magnetized Plasma Columns
authors: Roopendra Singh Rajawat And Gennady Shvets
abstract: Recent theoretical studies revealed the existence of topologically-protected surface plasma waves (TSPWs) in uniformly magnetized cold plasma columns. Reflections-free propagation of the TSPWs along arbitrarily-shaped plasma boundaries oriented perpendicularly to the magnetic field was shown to be preserved even when their collisionless damping by localized upper-hybrid resonances was accounted for. Here we extend this theory to the realistic case of three-dimensional magnetic field produced by finite-sized magnetic coils. We demonstrate that when TSPWs are launched in the direction of the decreasing magnetic field, they are collisionlessly absorbed within a highly localized (evanescent) region as they propagate away from the magnetic coil. We show that the resulting wave reflection can be negligible—in clear contrast with wave reflection from the corresponding evanescence regions of unmagnetized non-uniform plasmas.
tldr: This paper studies topologically-protected surface plasma waves in non-uniformly magnetized plasma columns, focusing on their propagation and collisionless damping.
motivation: To extend the theory of topologically-protected surface plasma waves from uniformly magnetized to realistic three-dimensional magnetic fields, and to understand their absorption and reflection properties.
method: The authors theoretically analyze wave propagation in a cold plasma column with a non-uniform magnetic field produced by finite-sized coils, using a model that accounts for collisionless damping by upper-hybrid resonances.
result: They find that waves launched in the direction of decreasing magnetic field are collisionlessly absorbed in a localized evanescent region, with negligible reflection, contrasting with unmagnetized non-uniform plasmas.
conclusion: The study demonstrates robust, reflection-free absorption of topologically-protected surface plasma waves in realistic non-uniform magnetic fields, which may have applications in plasma heating or wave manipulation.

title: Search For Decays Of The Higgs Boson Into Pair-produced Pseudoscalar Particles Decaying Into Τ + ...
authors: The ATLAS Collaboration
abstract: A search for a pair of low-mass pseudoscalars that promptly decay into -leptons is presented using 140 fb of proton–proton collision data at TeV centre-of-mass energy recorded with the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider. The result is used to place constraints on exotic decays of the Higgs boson into four -leptons, . This search focuses on events with either one or two -leptons decaying into hadrons and neutrinos, and the remaining three or two -leptons decaying into either electron or muon and neutrinos. No significant excess is observed above the expected Standard Model background and upper limits at the 95% confidence level on are set ranging from 0.06 to 0.23, depending on the mass ranging from 15 to 60 GeV.
tldr: This paper reports an ATLAS search for Higgs boson decays to pseudoscalars decaying to tau leptons, finding no significant excess and setting upper limits.
motivation: To probe exotic decays of the Higgs boson beyond the Standard Model, specifically decays into a pair of pseudoscalar particles that subsequently decay into tau leptons.
method: Analysis of 140 fb^-1 of proton-proton collision data at sqrt(s)=13 TeV recorded by the ATLAS detector, selecting events with one or two hadronically decaying taus and the remaining taus decaying to electrons or muons.
result: No significant excess over Standard Model background is observed; 95% CL upper limits on the branching ratio are set between 0.06 and 0.23 for pseudoscalar masses from 15 to 60 GeV.
conclusion: The search constrains exotic Higgs decays to four tau leptons, but does not fit the user's research interests in quantum information theory, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Causality Of Ultrafast Photoionization From Argon 3 S Usin...
authors: Rezvan Tahouri And Jan Marcus Dahlström
abstract: We study real-time photoionization flux at the Amusia–Cooper minimum (ACM) in argon using ab initio simulations with the relativistic time-dependent configuration-interaction singles (RTDCIS) method in length (LG) and velocity (VG) gauges. A simple analytical model is used to interpret the results, and to construct Wigner delays and Wigner distributions for both gauges and relativistic channels of the photoelectron ( with and ).
